title: Constructive Peter--Weyl Theory: What Is Known and What Remains Open
summary: What is known about constructive Peter-Weyl theory, and what remains open? This expository article separates established theorems, comparisons between formulations, and questions requiring further investigation in the Bishop-Coquand-Spitters line. Its central finding is that constructive Peter-Weyl theory already has an established compact-group approximation core: under specified analytic and Gelfand hypotheses, finite-rank central convolution projections converge strongly in the Haar L2 norm.
